body:
Review found that the deployed late-open cleanup could stop a long-lived connection during renegotiation. The reader sent a late close through `Session.write`, which waited for renegotiation to finish even though that same reader had to process its completion. A later review also found that repeated late replies could queue repeated close notices for one abandoned channel. This continues the BuildTest utilization and “out of date” campaign: a timed-out channel must release its later peer allocation while keeping the connection usable. The delta re-review then reproduced another bookkeeping gap: 64 outgoing opens whose socket writes failed before sending bytes left 64 reply ids retained on a connected session. The user asked to close the finding that the “expected-reply entry leaks when the outgoing channel-open write fails,” publish reader6, and update this pull request.

The final open decision and reply publication still share the channel monitor. The reader now retains only peer recipient integers under the outgoing packet lock. Renegotiation start, completion, queue insertion and queue drain use that lock; completion clears `in_kex` and sends each queued close once. Connection end marks the queue terminal and discards queued recipients. No product timeout, retry, extra worker or capacity bound was added. Each outgoing channel open stages its local reply id under the packet lock before the send. If `IO.put` throws, a `finally` block removes that id before releasing the same lock and preserves the original error. Successful sends retain their expected reply; failed attempts discard any subsequent reply, including a write failure after partial or complete delivery. The first confirmation or failure consumes that id. A first valid late confirmation queues one close notice; repeated replies and replies with no pending open take the diagnostic path and are ignored. Disconnect clears the expected ids with the deferred notices.

The public-API tests use a real local peer and the public socket factory. They hold actual confirmation bytes, hold the peer's renegotiation response separately, and observe a following peer notice through the public per-session logger. That proves the reader processed the late confirmation while renegotiation was still pending.

Coverage:

- `deferredCloseIsSentOnceAcrossConsecutiveRenegotiations`: two ordered renegotiations, one late allocation in each, no early close, exactly one close per peer recipient, and a following transport write.
- `connectionEndDiscardsDeferredClose`: a confirmed queued close while renegotiation remains pending, then public disconnect; zero close notices and zero remaining peer allocations after connection end.
- Existing reader-progress and late-open-failure controls: three first attempts each.
- Original `ChannelLateOpenTest`: all nine rows retained byte-for-byte.
- `repeatedLateConfirmationsProduceOneCloseAfterExchange`: 512 repeated replies plus an unknown local id while renegotiation is held; exactly one close notice after completion.
- `lateFailureConsumesExpectedReplyBeforeConfirmation`: an actual abandoned open receives a failure followed by a confirmation; zero close notices and a following transport write.
- Both `ChannelLateOpenTest.java` and `ChannelLateOpenRekeyTest.java` remain byte-identical to the preceding reviewed head.

Validation:

Latest failed-write correction:

- `FailedOpenReplyTest` uses the public socket factory and a real loopback peer. It covers 64 writes rejected before bytes, a one-byte partial write, and a complete write followed by a flush exception, three first attempts each. Exact caller errors, closed channels, a connected session, an unknown-id control and an ordered reader marker precede the reply diagnostic counts.
- Exact [the reviewed baseline](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/commit/48ad529432ac01a78c9c3a712be072a4e46b1c8c) product: **9/9 intended count failures**, three per scenario. Before-byte failures expected 64 ignored replies and observed 0; partial/flush cases expected 1 and observed 0. Final formatted tests with only the product restored: **9/9 intended count failures** again.
- Corrected targeted run: **36/36 first attempts**, comprising all 9 new rows plus the unchanged 27 neighbor rows. `ChannelLateOpenTest.java`, `ChannelLateOpenRekeyTest.java` and `PendingCloseBoundTest.java` remain byte-identical to [the reviewed baseline](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/commit/48ad529432ac01a78c9c3a712be072a4e46b1c8c).
- Final master full unit suite once: **534/534 first attempts**. Reader6 full unit suite and package once: **242/242 first attempts**. Zero failures/errors/skips/retry records in both and in the targeted gate.
- Independent test review and separate source/release review found no concrete blocker. The reader6 application preserves reader5 source lineage and its receive-credit guard. No existing test timeout, iteration, assertion or byte was changed in this lane.
- Global import validation passes; the unexcluded formatter retains the inherited protected-file complaint. Changed-file formatter validation passes. Native rows, full assertion stacks, review and publication checksums are on the [reader6 evidence branch](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/tree/wip/jschfix6-evidence).


Latest reply-consumption correction:

- Final fixture with exact previous product restored: **6/6 intended assertion failures**, repeated replies 3/3 observed 513 instead of 1 and failure-then-confirmation 3/3 observed 1 instead of 0; zero errors/skips/retry records.
- Corrected new tests: **6/6 first attempts**, three per scenario. Preserved lifecycle/rekey neighbors: **21/21 first attempts** on identical product and byte-identical test files.
- Final master full unit suite once: **525/525 first attempts**, zero failures/errors/skips/retry records. This retains all 519 prior rows and adds 6 reply-consumption rows.
- Final reader5 full unit suite and package once: **233/233 first attempts**, zero failures/errors/skips/retry records. This retains all 227 reader4 rows and adds the same 6 reply-consumption rows.
- Both protected test files remain byte-identical; changed-file formatting passes and all 401 files pass import validation. The unexcluded global formatter still reports only the protected lifecycle-file complaint described below.

Earlier deferred-close validation retained for context:

- Exact prior PR product ([prior product](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/commit/764cda9c)) with only the correction reversed: both new scenarios fail 3/3 at the reader-progress assertions, six intended failures and zero errors/skips/retry records. The later queue-drop assertions are reachable only after the corrected reader progresses.
- Reader3 publication base: the same six intended failures, each new scenario red 3/3.
- Corrected master product: full Maven unit suite once, **519/519** first attempts; final targeted gate **21/21**, with zero failures/errors/skips/retry records. That 519-row suite used the same product as reader4; the later test-only changes concerned cleanup order and formatting.
- Reader4 publication suite: **227/227** first attempts; zero failures/errors/skips/retry records, including all 12 renegotiation rows, nine lifecycle rows and eight receive-flow rows.
- Independent source and test review completed, including the reader3-based application. Review's fixture cleanup findings were addressed.

Formatting validation remains blocked by the unchanged protected lifecycle file. The repository formatter requests whitespace changes in `ChannelLateOpenTest.java`; this brief explicitly requires that file to remain byte-identical. The changed files pass formatting and all 401 files pass import validation. No validator exclusion was added. The [evidence branch](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/tree/wip/jschfix3-evidence) contains the exact failure and an external formatted copy for the orchestrator to resolve that requirement.

Reader5 test-fixture correction: The first corrected local target run exposed an intermittent missing following write in `PendingCloseBoundTest`. A diagnostic batch using eight real concurrent client/peer pairs observed peer setup errors in 10/100 scenarios. The fixture had replayed a held proposal outside the peer decoder lock, allowing a reply before setup finished. Replaying under the same lock and normal handler context passed 100/100 first attempts; all existing waits, 512 replies, and exact-count assertions remain. The final fixture still fails 6/6 on the old product and passes 6/6 with the correction. Complete native XML and stacks are on the [evidence branch](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/tree/wip/jschfix5-evidence).

Existing-test edits: `ChannelLateOpenTest.java` unchanged (SHA-256 `eb523698b133d41a85650bab5650a7da18e282ce3c5d6b0720199f98689835d5`). `ChannelLateOpenRekeyTest.java` gains the two scenarios and fixture gates/counts/cleanup; its original assertions are retained and its imports/layout are formatted. No existing timeout or iteration count changed.

Reader6 publication: `com.github.mwiede:jsch:0.2.18-reader6`, published with publisher 0.0.6 after an immediate 404 POM probe. Its [POM](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader6/jsch-0.2.18-reader6.pom), [library jar](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader6/jsch-0.2.18-reader6.jar), [sources jar](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader6/jsch-0.2.18-reader6-sources.jar) and [Javadoc jar](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader6/jsch-0.2.18-reader6-javadoc.jar) return 200 and match local SHA-256. All 285 checked-in Java sources match; base classes remain Java 8, no peer/test/dependency classes are bundled, and dependency declarations match reader5. [Release source](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/commit/74923e5073b553e9512029e01ab19ee311b1abe2); [public retrieval/checksum record](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/blob/wip/jschfix6-evidence/evidence/jschfix6-publication-verification.json).

Reader5 publication: `com.github.mwiede:jsch:0.2.18-reader5`, published with publisher 0.0.6 after an immediate 404 POM preprobe. The [POM](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader5/jsch-0.2.18-reader5.pom), [library jar](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader5/jsch-0.2.18-reader5.jar), [sources jar](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader5/jsch-0.2.18-reader5-sources.jar) and [Javadoc jar](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader5/jsch-0.2.18-reader5-javadoc.jar) each return 200 and match local SHA-256. All 285 checked-in Java sources match the sources jar; the base class format remains Java 8, no test/peer/dependency classes are bundled, and dependency declarations match reader4. The [release source](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/commit/ae0fffafae970cd1abe760ec8c4d8b5bc6ebfe13) preserves reader4 lineage and receive behavior. [Retrieval/checksum evidence](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/blob/wip/jschfix5-evidence/evidence/jschfix5-publication-verification.json).

Earlier publication: `com.github.mwiede:jsch:0.2.18-reader4`, published with publisher 0.0.6. The [public POM](https://kotlin.directory/com/github/mwiede/jsch/0.2.18-reader4/jsch-0.2.18-reader4.pom), library jar, sources jar and Javadoc jar return 200 and match local SHA-256 values. The [release source](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/tree/wip/jschfix3-reader4) preserves reader3's receive implementation and dependency declarations, with the same deferred-close correction. All 285 checked-in Java sources match its published sources; the base library remains Java 8 compatible.

CI: the required `kotlin.build (remote)` check is successful on [the tested head](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/commit/7a7f397cff5006cd3373940b8b004ed80560dd29). The orchestrator clarified at 03:48 UTC that `kotlin.build (kompile-remote-build)` is informational and is not a gate for this lane; its absent dispatch and the watcher behavior are recorded in the [findings](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jsch/blob/wip/jschfix5-evidence/evidence/jschfix5-findings.md). No merge or enqueue was performed; the reader6 lane also stops at the required remote check and does not wait for the informational check.

The inherited channel-id reuse finding is recorded under `FOLLOW-UP` with source anchors in the evidence findings. Reply tracking still uses local numeric ids and does not solve reassignment after 2^31 constructions. It needs a separate allocator lifecycle correction and a public-API failing-first test; it is not mixed into this change. The pull request remains open for orchestrator review.
